subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw expose a core web-tool domain egress policy, and if so should it be limited to a `web_fetch` hostname allowlist or cover managed/native search, provider fallback, browser, proxy, redirect, and cache paths too?
rationale: This is a public operator-trusted security boundary and the current related PRs encode different answers, so automation should not choose the permanent policy shape without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Pause local `web_fetch` config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Require cross-tool design first
options.body: Hold implementation until a single design covers fetch, search, browser, provider fallback, redirects, caches, plugin HTTP, and proxy-routed egress.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the SSRF, guarded fetch, and web_fetch runtime surfaces involved in this boundary choice.
